title: Correlated Columns and Multi-Column Extended Statistics (CREATE STATISTICS)
realWorldScenario: A query filtering `WHERE make = 'Audi' AND model = 'R8'` estimates that 1 row will match, but in reality 85,000 rows match. Because of this massive misestimation, PostgreSQL chooses a disastrous Nested Loop instead of a Hash Join, taking 45 seconds.
questionStatement: Explain how PostgreSQL computes selectivity for multi-column WHERE clauses by default. Why does the conditional independence assumption fail for correlated data? How does `CREATE STATISTICS` (dependencies, ndistinct, mcv) resolve multi-column cardinality estimation errors?
expectedConcepts: Conditional independence assumption: P(A and B) = P(A) * P(B)
Planner picking nested loop due to 1-row estimation
CREATE STATISTICS syntax with dependencies, mcv, and ndistinct
Mandatory ANALYZE step to populate the statistics object
hints: Why does multiplying two probabilities underestimate matching rows when columns are correlated?
What happens to join selection when the planner expects 1 row instead of 85,000?
